AuthnAdminDomainClaim.description: A domain to claim for one identity provider.

domain.description: The domain to claim, for example example.com; it is trimmed and lower-cased before it is stored.

AuthnAdminMember.description: One account's membership in one tenant.

active.description: True when the membership is in force; false means suspended, which reads as not a member.

display_name.description: The account's display name, at most 100 characters and not used for any decision; the empty string when the account has none.

joined_at.description: When the account joined the tenant, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

roles.description: The role names the account holds in the tenant, ascending and without duplicates; always an array and never null, empty when it holds none.

source.description: How the membership came to exist: admin, initial, invite, import or jit:<provider identifier>.

sso_exempt.description: True when the member is exempt from the tenant's enforced SSO requirement.

AuthnAdminMemberList.description: One page of a tenant's memberships, in ascending account-identifier order, and the cursor of the next page.

members.description: The memberships on this page; the empty array when the tenant has none.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, empty on the last page

AuthnAdminMemberSSOExempt.description: A member's exemption from the tenant's enforced SSO requirement.

sso_exempt.description: True exempts the member; false clears the exemption.

AuthnAdminMemberWrite.description: A membership write: whether the account is an active member of the tenant and whether the tenant's SSO requirement exempts it.

active.description: True adds or resumes the membership; false suspends it, and a suspended membership reads as not a member.

source.description: Absent records the change as an administrator's

sso_exempt.description: True exempts the member from the tenant's enforced SSO requirement.

AuthnAdminProvider.description: One SSO provider. The encrypted client secret never appears, warnings names each setting that loosens a default, and domains lists every email domain the provider has claimed.

allow_idp_initiated.description: True when an unsolicited assertion from the provider is accepted; the route then warns that login CSRF cannot be defended against.

allow_sha1.description: True when SHA-1 signed assertions are accepted; the route then warns about the downgrade.

config.description: The protocol's own configuration; absent when the provider carries none

domains.description: Every email domain the provider has claimed, verified or not, in ascending domain order; always an array and never null, empty when it has none.

enabled.description: True when the provider may be used for sign-in.

merge_existing.description: The stored merge flag; it no longer opens merging, because a just-in-time login never merges into an existing account.

name.description: The provider's display name; 1 to 64 characters.

provisioning.description: jit creates an account on first sign-in; preprovisioned matches only an account an administrator has already created.

tenant.description: The owning tenant's identifier; immutable after creation.

trust_idp_mfa.description: True when the provider's assertion may count as a multi-factor proof, and only when its acr (or SAML AuthnContextClassRef) is in the configured list.

username_claim.description: The claim a claim strategy reads: preferred_username or email (the address's local part). Empty for every other strategy.

username_strategy.description: How a jit login determines the username it opens the account with: claim reads username_claim from the assertion, user-confirm asks the person before any account is written. Empty for a preprovisioned provider.

version.description: The provider's version, raised by every write.

warnings.description: Absent when no setting loosens a default

AuthnAdminProviderDomain.description: One email domain a provider has claimed, and whether its ownership was proved.

domain.description: The domain in its normalized form: lower-case ASCII (punycode).

verified.description: True when the domain's DNS TXT record proved ownership; only verified domains take part in sign-in discovery.

AuthnAdminProviderEnvelope.description: A response carrying one SSO provider.

AuthnAdminProviderList.description: The SSO providers of one tenant.

providers.description: The tenant's providers; the empty array when it has none.

AuthnAdminProviderWrite.description: An identity provider as an administrator creates or updates it: the protocol, the provisioning mode and the protocol's own configuration.

allow_idp_initiated.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

allow_sha1.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

client_secret.description: Absent writes no client secret on a create and keeps the stored one on an update

enabled.description: Absent leaves the enabled flag as it is (false on a create)

merge_existing.description: The stored merge flag; absent leaves it as it is (false on a create). It no longer opens merging into an existing account.

name.description: The provider's display name; 1 to 64 characters.

protocol.description: The protocol: oidc or saml. The set is closed.

provisioning.description: jit creates an account on first sign-in; preprovisioned matches only an account an administrator has already created. Required, with no default.

tenant.description: Absent on a create takes the path's tenant; a value that names another is refused

trust_idp_mfa.description: Absent leaves the flag as it is (false on a create)

username_claim.description: The claim a claim strategy reads: preferred_username or email (the address's local part). Required on a create when the strategy is claim; absent keeps the stored value on an update; empty for every other strategy.

username_strategy.description: How a jit login determines the username: claim or user-confirm. Required on a create when provisioning is jit; absent keeps the stored value on an update; empty for preprovisioned, and a claim strategy requires username_claim.

AuthnAdminVerifyToken.description: The token to publish in DNS to verify a claimed domain.

verify_token.description: The token to publish in DNS

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Lists one tenant's memberships, one page at a time, in ascending account-identifier order, and answers the cursor of the next page. Each member carries the roles the account holds in the tenant and the instant it joined. An optional role parameter narrows the page to the members bound to that role name, matched exactly, and combines with the text query; an unknown role name selects no member rather than failing. The path names the tenant identifier itself, not an alias: the module holds no tenant roster and does not look the tenant up, and the same identifier is the decision's tenant. Requires membership.manage.

parameters.description: Narrows the page to the members whose account display name or login identifiers begin with this text; absent or empty selects every member. The display name is matched as a byte prefix of the stored value, and an identifier after the query is lower-cased, the form usernames and email addresses are stored in.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Narrows the page to the members holding this role name in the tenant, matched exactly; absent or empty selects every member. A name no role of the tenant uses selects no member and is still a 200, so the parameter does not reveal which role names exist. A role filter needs the policy module's member role reader; an assembly without one answers 503.
parameters.name: role

parameters.description: The page size. Absent or 0 takes the default of 100; a value above 1000 is capped at 1000 rather than refused; a negative or non-integer value is 400.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page, or empty for the first page. The cursor is the account identifier of the last matching membership on that page.
parameters.name: after

parameters.description: The tenant's identifier (the tenant module's ID as a string), not an alias or a display name.
parameters.name: tenant

400.description: The page query could not be read

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller may not read memberships

delete.description: Removes the account's membership from the tenant. Requires membership.manage with the path's tenant. The route is idempotent: a membership that is not there is already removed, and the call answers 204.

parameters.description: The tenant's identifier (the tenant module's ID as a string), not an alias or a display name.
parameters.name: tenant

parameters.description: The account's identifier: 1 to 64 bytes from [A-Za-z0-9._-], case-sensitive.
parameters.name: account

400.description: The tenant or account identifier is invalid

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller may not remove memberships

409.description: The membership cannot be removed in its current state

delete.summary: Remove an account's membership from a tenant

put.description: Writes one account's membership in one tenant: active true adds or resumes it and active false suspends it, and a suspended membership reads as no membership. source records how it came to exist; omitted records it as an administrator's change. The account must exist and not be a tombstone. An administrator cannot suspend their own membership: that is a 409 cannot-suspend-self, while another administrator may suspend them. Requires membership.manage with the path's tenant.

parameters.description: The tenant's identifier (the tenant module's ID as a string), not an alias or a display name.
parameters.name: tenant

parameters.description: The account's identifier: 1 to 64 bytes from [A-Za-z0-9._-], case-sensitive.
parameters.name: account

requestBody.description: The membership to write. active, sso_exempt and source are all optional on the wire, but an absent active writes false, which suspends the membership.

400.description: The body could not be read, an unknown field included, the tenant is invalid, or source is longer than 128 bytes. The module has no role.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller may not write memberships

409.description: The caller cannot suspend their own membership

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

put.summary: Write an account's membership in a tenant

put.description: Sets or clears a member's emergency exemption from the tenant's enforced SSO requirement. The membership must already exist: an absent one is 404, and the route changes only the exemption, leaving the rest of the membership as it is. Requires membership.manage.

parameters.description: The account's identifier: 1 to 64 bytes from [A-Za-z0-9._-], case-sensitive.

requestBody.description: The exemption flag to write; false clears the exemption.

post.description: Creates an SSO provider in the tenant. The path and the body must agree on the tenant: an absent body tenant takes the path's, and a different one is 400. protocol is oidc or saml; provisioning is jit or preprovisioned and has no default. A jit provider names username_strategy, claim or user-confirm; a claim strategy names username_claim, preferred_username or email, and no other strategy carries one. A client secret is carried only by an OIDC provider. Every write raises the provider's version. Requires idp.manage.

parameters.description: The tenant's identifier (the tenant module's ID as a string), not an alias or a display name.
parameters.name: tenant

requestBody.description: The provider to create. protocol, name, provisioning and config are required; username_strategy is required when provisioning is jit, username_claim when the strategy is claim, and an incomplete or unknown combination is refused; the config is validated against the protocol and an unknown key is refused.

A jit provider names username_strategy, claim or user-confirm; a claim strategy names username_claim, preferred_username or email, and no other strategy carries one. Booleans, username_strategy and username_claim left out keep their stored value, and an omitted client_secret keeps the stored one. The tenant is immutable: a body naming another tenant is 400. Requires idp.manage; each write raises version.
